evidence: The frozen workbook Quality Checks!D3 asks for an authentic human voice, and Internal Quality Checks!D3 adds no contrary annotation. The brief opens with a concrete personal use case ('I often paste a long one-line experiment') and a natural concern about another tab saving first (task/instruction.md:1), then makes a concise request to read the notes and build the app (task/instruction.md:3-5). The notes use short, direct product language such as 'The editor should be a useful tool in its own right' (environment/instructions/overview.md:5), 'Keep the latest successful preview as a last-good picture' (environment/instructions/behaviour.md:5), and 'You may choose the layout, labels, routes, database schema and error wording' (environment/instructions/policy.md:3). The long editor detail at ui.md:3-17 is specific technical guidance in the same plain voice, without generic marketing gloss or an abrupt persona change. This is an input-prose check: a broken app could still receive this Pass, and a working app would not repair an unnatural instruction; no app run is needed to establish the written voice.
